Thanks for the context — tagging in the tax guidance here so operations can proceed cleanly. Short checklist and sample text below.

Checklist (what we need to clear reverse-charge and reissue net invoice):
- Valid VAT ID for the buying entity (VIES screenshot or VAT registration certificate).
- Confirmation of the invoiced legal entity (DE GmbH vs UK Ltd) and billing address.
- Copy of the original invoice lines and amounts (Marissa, we have INV-20250701).

Technical points:
- If buyer is a VAT-registered business in an EU member state (DE) and supplier is non-EU or different EU state, reverse-charge typically applies and Redwood should issue a net invoice with 0% VAT and a reference to the reverse-charge rule.
- If buyer is UK-registered and supply is to UK, UK VAT rules apply (make sure GB ID validates).

Suggested invoice wording (please use exact phrasing when reissuing):
"Supply of cloud inference services — B2B reverse charge applies. VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Article 194 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC (or local equivalent). Recipient VAT ID: [BUYER_VAT_ID]. Supplier VAT ID: Redwood Inference EU VAT ID: EU123456789."

Invoice line items: show net amounts, then a separate line: "VAT (reverse-charge) — customer to account for VAT under reverse-charge rules" — and leave VAT column as 0.00 with a note.

Retention: keep the VAT cert + VIES screenshot attached to the invoice record for audit (we store in Finance Drive).

Marissa: once Andrew confirms the buyer entity and attaches the cert, please issue a corrected invoice with the wording above, attach Aquila's VAT cert, and mark the invoice as "Reissued — reverse-charge" in our system.
